artifact.type: frozen local Web, backend, iOS, browser-extension, and Codex-plugin system

scenario: Frozen synthetic TS-CORE-01 is reviewed across the local Web and backend receipt path, direct iPhone 17 Simulator, exact unpacked extension package, and installed personal Codex plugin without live candidate data or external writes.

review_plan.reason: The artifact must complete one low-friction recruiter evidence-to-action workflow.
Capture permission, payload truth, retention, deletion, account scope, and external-write authority are release gates.
The frozen product includes a directly verified iOS surface with interruption and accessibility requirements.
Candidate conversation handling must remain deliberate, respectful, transparent, and reversible.
Workflow facts must not become person scores, ranking, fit, personality, protected-trait, or acceptance claims.

reviews.lens: time-constrained recruiter task completion, evidence review, decision clarity, recovery, and inspectable cross-surface outcomes

findings.observation: The frozen system now has direct Web, Simulator, automated extension-package, backend, and installed-plugin evidence, but no uncoached recruiter completed the one remaining visible Google Chrome capture path and explained every authority transition.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-3/final/localhost-web-retention.json, docs/evaluations/round-3/final/ios-simulator.json, docs/evaluations/round-3/final/browser-extension.json, and docs/evaluations/round-3/final/codex-plugin.json record the verified surfaces; browser-extension.json keeps XS-CAPTURE-01 active.
findings.user_impact: The review workflow is executable, but first-use evidence does not yet prove that a recruiter will distinguish capture receipt, fact confirmation, action approval, and verified outcome without coaching.
findings.recommendation: Run the single selected-text Chrome walkthrough on the exact frozen unpacked package and ask the recruiter to narrate the boundaries without prompting.
findings.verification: A first-time recruiter selects the synthetic TS-CORE-01 sentence, invokes the toolbar, sees the exact preview, observes no pre-Submit POST, submits once, and correctly explains the same-account receipt and readback.

strengths: The real Web handoff returned one account-scoped receipt; its duplicate reused the same capture and receipt, and workspace readback kept four new proposals at zero newly confirmed facts.
The direct iPhone 17 Simulator run exercised confirm, edit, dismiss, separate action preview, and a local no-external-write outcome.
The extension preserves evidence, local-session readiness, explicit approval, Submit, and receipt as separate steps while visible-tab image submission fails closed.
No candidate contact, calendar, message, ATS, CRM, or other external write was attempted.
missing_evidence: One uncoached recruiter walkthrough through the visible user Google Chrome capture boundary.
A field timing comparison against the recruiter's current manual workflow.
open_questions: After the manual capture gate passes, is reviewing four same-source facts individually still faster than one evidence inspection followed by an explicit batch decision?

reviews.lens: intentional capture, payload-shape truth, provenance, identity and account scope, authorization, retention, deletion, and truthful lineage

findings.observation: The exact MV3 package passes source, built-package, manifest, pre-Submit, explicit-Submit, and synthetic receipt checks, but this run did not load and invoke it through the user's visible Google Chrome chrome://extensions and toolbar or selected-text gesture, so a positive temporary activeTab grant remains unproven.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-3/final/browser-extension.json freezes package sha256 a7f69be69a069897a122a7676d12bbd6e9246392d03d05a0c733e4b56deb6314 and explicitly distinguishes automated Chromium from the missing user Google Chrome permission boundary.
findings.user_impact: Without the direct permission trace, the evaluation cannot prove that candidate evidence enters only after the promised visible, source-scoped recruiter gesture.
findings.recommendation: Load the exact package digest in the user's visible Google Chrome, use selected-text capture on synthetic TS-CORE-01, and record the permission-to-receipt trace.
findings.verification: One direct trace shows the enabled package, toolbar or selected-text gesture, positive activeTab, exact reviewed text, zero capture POST before Submit, one explicit Submit, and one same-account localhost receipt and workspace readback.

strengths: The backend now binds reviewed_selected_text to a transcript containing exactly one sequence-zero message and rejects multi-message claims before persistence.
Every reviewed_evidence_crop request now fails closed because no governed crop bytes or asset lifecycle reaches the backend; the Web selected-text path remains accepted as reviewed_selected_text.

The fresh 001-to-002 historical migration scrubs legacy active source, evidence, proposals, source metadata, and replay caches; it records legacy_unknown, source_purged_at, source_purged, and legacy_unverified at one truthful timestamp while preserving deleted-row semantics.
Fresh Docker retention evaluation proves ephemeral purge, evidence expiry and purge, duplicate idempotency, cross-account isolation, deletion lineage, and non-restoration from retry caches.
The real Web receipt and workspace readback are account-scoped and keep evidence, proposal, historical confirmed state, approval, authority, and outcome distinct.
missing_evidence: Direct visible user Google Chrome load, selected-text invocation, positive activeTab grant, pre-Submit network silence, and extension-originated same-account receipt/readback.
vetoes: XS-CAPTURE-01: the intentional user Google Chrome selected-text capture and pre-Submit silence boundary is unproven.
XS-RETENTION-01: payload-shape enforcement, legacy migration truth, expiry, purge, deletion lineage, and retry-cache scrubbing required independent re-verification.
open_questions: What candidate-facing notice and deletion route will be required before the system is ever allowed to process non-synthetic conversation evidence?

reviews.lens: iOS task completion, touch and accessibility layout, state semantics, backend parity, interruption, failure, cancellation, and recovery

findings.observation: The current iPhone 17 Simulator build passed AX ordering and an AX5 dark-mode accessibility audit, but no VoiceOver traversal was executed in this run.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-3/final/ios-simulator.json records 13/13 unit tests, the corrected final 12/12 UI suite, direct Simulator decisions and screenshots, and voiceover_tested=false.
findings.user_impact: Large-text, dark, touch, interruption, failure, and cancellation paths have direct evidence while a VoiceOver user may still encounter an unclear spoken order or state change.
findings.recommendation: Run a truthful VoiceOver traversal of the frozen TS-CORE-01 evidence, decisions, action preview, local outcome, and recovery states.
findings.verification: VoiceOver announces identity, provenance, proposed versus confirmed state, edit and dismiss outcomes, exact target and effect, no-external-change result, and retry in logical order without duplicate or ambiguous controls.

strengths: The isolated unit suite passed 13/13 and the final full UI suite passed 12/12 on the authorized iPhone 17 Simulator with separate DerivedData.

A timing-dependent cancellation test first failed, was corrected with a validated test-only launch delay while preserving the two-second product default, then passed both targeted and full-suite reruns.
The direct Simulator walkthrough confirmed two facts, dismissed one, edited and confirmed one, then preserved a separate action preview and local no-external-write outcome.
AX5 dark mode, evidence ordering, backend parity, interruption, failure, cancellation, stale preview, offline recovery, scoring refusal, and unrelated-image handling match the frozen evidence.
A separate Release simulator build succeeded with code signing disabled.
missing_evidence: A current VoiceOver spoken-order and control-state transcript.
open_questions: Does the same evidence-to-decision order remain efficient on the smallest supported iPhone?

reviews.lens: human-first handling of candidate evidence, respectful interpretation, transparency, restraint, and reversible recruiter-owned action

findings.observation: Every evaluated surface labels TS-CORE-01 as synthetic, keeps exact evidence beside proposals, and requires a separate decision, but the user's visible Google Chrome selected-text gesture and temporary permission grant are still not recorded.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-3/final/browser-extension.json records the exact package, pre-Submit synthetic silence, explicit synthetic Submit, and the active XS-CAPTURE-01 boundary.
findings.user_impact: Downstream handling is restrained, but the run cannot yet prove that a conversation enters only through the visible, deliberate recruiter gesture promised to protect candidate context.
findings.recommendation: Complete the single manual selected-text Chrome trace with synthetic evidence and keep the exact reviewed text visible through explicit Submit.
findings.verification: The recording shows the chosen synthetic text, positive temporary activeTab, no earlier handoff, one Submit, and no access to other tabs, history, cookies, or external systems.

strengths: The system records evidence-backed situational facts and never ranks candidate worth, personality, protected traits, culture fit, or acceptance probability.
Exact evidence, proposals, recruiter decisions, historical confirmed state, action authority, and observed outcome remain visibly distinct.
No-action, ambiguity, retraction, identity, consent, and prohibited-scoring fixtures prevent manufactured urgency and unsupported interpretation.
No candidate contact, calendar, message, ATS, CRM, or other external write was attempted.
Retention receipts and legacy lineage now avoid claiming more source completeness than the system can prove.
missing_evidence: Direct user Google Chrome capture-permission and selected-text review recording.
Candidate-facing notice, consent, access, and deletion-route evaluation remains outside this synthetic recruiter-only slice.
open_questions: What plain-language notice and deletion path should a candidate receive before any real conversation evidence can enter this system?

reviews.lens: job-relevant evidence boundaries, calibrated uncertainty, prohibited person scoring, and separation of workflow attention from selection judgment
strengths: TS-CORE-01 contains source-bound workflow facts and a recruiter-owned clarification proposal, not a candidate score, rank, personality inference, culture-fit label, or acceptance probability.
All eight fixtures and 13 backend failure boundaries preserve ambiguity, reject prohibited scoring, and keep proposed interpretation separate from confirmed state.
The installed plugin passes 8/8 fixtures and all three identity, authorization, and speaker probes with execution_authority=none, confirmed_state_changed=false, and external_effect=not_attempted.
Web, iOS, browser-extension, backend, and plugin evidence preserve the same proposal-only selection boundary.
Legacy retention correction reduces evidentiary overclaiming by representing unverified historical completeness as legacy_unknown rather than full reviewed source.

top_findings.next_step: Run the one remaining manual Chrome gate on the exact frozen package.
top_findings.verification: Visible chrome://extensions load, selected-text or toolbar gesture, positive activeTab, exact preview, pre-Submit silence, explicit Submit, and same-account receipt/readback all appear in one trace.

top_findings.reason: AX5 dark and accessibility ordering pass, but no VoiceOver traversal was executed.
top_findings.next_step: Record the frozen evidence-to-outcome sequence with VoiceOver.
top_findings.verification: Spoken identity, evidence, proposal, decision, action preview, no-external-change outcome, and recovery remain logical and unambiguous.

agreements: Evidence, proposal, confirmed state, action approval, execution authority, and observed outcome remain separate.
The retention implementation now fails closed for false minimized scopes and reports legacy purge truthfully.
No surface ranks candidate worth, personality, culture fit, protected traits, or acceptance probability.
No candidate contact, calendar, message, ATS, CRM, or other external write was attempted.
High Web and extension craft scores cannot override an active evidence-safety veto.

veto_resolution.veto: XS-CAPTURE-01: the intentional user Google Chrome selected-text capture and pre-Submit silence boundary is unproven.
veto_resolution.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-3/final/browser-extension.json proves the exact automated package behavior but explicitly lacks the user Google Chrome chrome://extensions, selected-text gesture, positive activeTab, real pre-Submit trace, and extension-originated same-account receipt/readback.

veto_resolution.veto: XS-RETENTION-01: payload-shape enforcement, legacy migration truth, expiry, purge, deletion lineage, and retry-cache scrubbing required independent re-verification.
veto_resolution.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-3/final/localhost-backend-retention.json and legacy-migration.json directly prove single-message selected-text success, multi-message and all crop rejection, ephemeral and deadline purge, duplicate and cross-account behavior, deletion lineage, legacy_unknown scrubbing, truthful purge time and lineage, and no raw-text restoration from retry caches.

adjudication.rationale: All deterministic compiler, backend, Web, iOS, extension, plugin, retention, and documentation gates pass after two disclosed integration corrections. XS-RETENTION-01 is resolved by independent fresh-Docker and historical-migration evidence. XS-CAPTURE-01 remains active because automated Chromium cannot substitute for the user's visible Google Chrome permission boundary. Veto-first adjudication therefore requires verdict=fail and release_gate=block; the preserved 95–99 craft scores are not averaged into a pass.
